ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure contains multiple index curves changing with “time after maturation/d”. The legend in the lower right shows that the solid-point curve represents variety A, and the hollow-point curve represents variety B. In the upper-left “hardness” graph, the hardness of variety A decreases as the time after maturation extends, but it decreases more slowly, and still maintains relatively high hardness at 20 days; the hardness of variety B decreases faster and approaches a lower level in the later period. Then reason: The stem states that after peach fruits mature, if they soften quickly, their storage and transportation resistance is poor. A slow decrease in hardness indicates slow softening, so storage and transportation resistance is better. In the figure, the hardness of variety A decreases more slowly, so the variety resistant to storage and transportation is A.
